entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Prateek Maheshwari - Advocate for the appellant.
Shri Ajay Raj Gupta - Panel Lawyer for respondent/

Stat
Heard on the question of admission.
Appeals is admitted for final hearing.
Both the parties are also heard on I.A. No.5228 of 2023, which is an application under Section 389 of Cr.P.C. for suspension of remaining jail sentence and grant of bail on behalf of sole appellant.

2. Appellant has been convicted under Sections 498A and 304 of IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act and has been sentenced to undergo 2 years S.I. with fine of Rs.2,000/-, 7 years S.I.
with fine of Rs.2,000/- and 1 year S.I. with fine of Rs.1,000/- respectively with usual default stipulation.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this matter.
He is the husband of deceased, but he never physically or mentally harassed the deceased or abetted her to commit suicide.
He never made any demand of dowry or committed cruelty on deceased.
No previous complaint has been made against him by the parents of the deceased prior to the incident.
The statement of complainant (PW-1 and PW-2) do not inspire confidence.
Learned trial Court disbelieved major part of prosecution story and acquitted all other accused persons in same matter.
Appellant has a minor child of 9 years of age, who is suffering some medical ailments.
Mother of appellant is also too aged lady to look after the minor child.
Appellant is a sole bread earner of his family.
Looking to old pendency of the cases for consideration, final conclusion of this appeal would take sufficient long time.
There is a strong case in favour of the appellant.
Hence, the execution of the remaining part of the jail sentence of the appellant be suspended till the final disposal of this appeal.

4. In support of his contention, learned counsel for the appellant placed reliance upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kuljit Singh and Anr. Vs. State of Punjab reported in (2022) 1 Abhishek @ Bunty vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38408600/
1 SCC 385; Raman Kumar Vs. State of Punjab reported in (2009) 16 SCC 35 and Nepal Singh Vs. State of Haryana reported in (2009) 12 SCC 351.
5.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the application for suspension of sentence and prays for its rejection.

6. Perused the judgment of the trial Court as well as the statement of Arpit Yadav, brother of the deceased (PW-1), Asha Yadav, mother of the deceased (PW-2), Archana Yadav, relative of the deceased (PW-3) and Narendra Yadav, other relative of the deceased (PW-4) deposed against the appellant by stating that after marriage present appellant has mentally and physically harassed the deceased for non-fulfilment of demand of dowry.
Deceased
was died within 7 years of her marriage.
She had committed suicide by hanging herself in the house of appellant.

All these witnesses deposed that some days prior to the incident, Mundan Ceremony of son of the deceased was performed and appellant and his family members was annoying the deceased that her family members did not give any golden ornament in the Mundan Ceremony, due to which she was mentally and physically harassed by them.
7.
In view of the evidence available on record, at this stage, this Court is not inclined to allow the application.
8. Accordingly, I.A. No.5228 of 2023 is rejected 9.
Registry is directed to list the appeal for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Anushree Abhishek @ Bunty vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38408600/
